encounters.cc: Admitted for elective right hemicolectomy; postoperative day 1 with surgical site pain and reluctance to deep breathe or cough.

lines: Admitted for elective right hemicolectomy; postoperative day 1 with surgical site pain and reluctance to deep breathe or cough.

The patient is a 68-year-old male with COPD, hypertension, and type 2 diabetes mellitus who was diagnosed with right-sided colon cancer one month prior and returns on postoperative day 1 following right hemicolectomy.
The surgery is uneventful, and he is transferred to postoperative care.
He complains of moderate pain at the surgical site, rating 6 out of 10 on the pain scale.
He is reluctant to take deep breaths or cough due to the pain.
- Right hemicolectomy with ileocolic anastomosis for colonic adenocarcinoma

lines: Found unresponsive at home after one week of increasing lethargy and progressive difficulty breathing.
This 71-year-old male with COPD and respiratory complications presents.
His family reports that he has been increasingly lethargic over the past week and has had difficulty breathing today.
- Right hemicolectomy with ileocolic anastomosis for colonic adenocarcinoma

The patient's daughter provides a document that she found in his belongings, which appears to be a living will stating the patient's desire to avoid mechanical ventilation or resuscitative efforts in the event of severe illness.
The family is divided on whether to honor the document, with some members insisting on full resuscitative measures.
His vitals are: BP 90/60 mmHg, HR 118 bpm, RR 30/min, T 37.8°C, and SpO2 88% on room air.
